maria.dev: Pushed a kernel-priority selector tweak to canary (priority_weight heuristic) ~10m ago. Noticing p99 climb for redwood/base-7b-quant on the canary slice. I’m rolling it back now.

aj: Which percentile is spiking? p95 or p99? Any change in CPU or queue depth?

maria.dev: Mostly p99, p95 nudge only. Dashboard shows tail latency +220ms on 1s baseline. CPU flat, but queue depth spiked briefly. KV cache miss rate also increased in the same timeframe.

lee: Confirming KV miss ups. Prefetch-window was effectively reduced after the selector change — fewer prefix hits, more cold KV fetches.

diane: Any observed microbatching differences? Could the selector be pushing more tiny-microbatches to hit hot-path kernels?

maria.dev: Yes — profiler shows higher small-seq kernel usage and microbatch sizes collapsed for 90% of requests. Looks like priority_weight favors low-latency kernels that don't coalesce well.

runtime-bot: Perf profile snapshot (canary-2026-03-17 22:10):
```
model: redwood/base-7b-quant
p99_inc: +220ms
avg_microbatch_size: 1.6 -> 1.02
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.12 -> 0.37
kernel_hotpath: smallseq_fast (increase)
queue_depth_95: 3 -> 12
kv_fetch_latency_avg: 8ms -> 42ms
```

sre-oncall: This is crossing the SLO alert threshold for some customers. If you have a rollback plan, do it now.

maria.dev: Initiating hot revert. Disabling the new priority_weight heuristic and restoring previous selector config. Running revert command: `revert-deploy --service=runtime-selector --to=stable-2026-03-10`

deploy-bot: Revert started by maria.dev. Canary update in progress.

aj: Also disable adaptive microbatching on canary for a minute to rule out interaction. `runtimectl set-config --canary adaptive_microbatch=false`

maria.dev: Done. Revert applied and adaptive microbatch disabled. Watching metrics.

runtime-bot: Canary metrics (2m after revert): p99 = baseline + 18ms, avg_microbatch_size = 1.6, kv_cache_miss_rate = 0.13, queue_depth_95 = 4.

deploy-bot: Revert completed and promoted to canary stable.

sre-oncall: Nice — SLOs recovering. Please follow-up with postmortem and a test harness that simulates KV cold start behavior.

diane: I'll file a short incident note and add a regression test that simulates skewed prefix distributions + canary traffic.

lee: Root cause hypothesis: priority_weight change reduces batching by biasing toward low-latency kernel selection, inadvertently increasing KV miss and RPC fetch tail. Fix options: tweak weight, add a min_microbatch_size floor, or make selector KV-aware (prefer kernels that preserve prefix coalescing).

aj: Also add a canary probe that measures kv_cache_hit_rate and microbatch_size distribution before promoting selector changes.

maria.dev: Agreed. Creating follow-up tickets and will schedule a short postmortem. Thanks for quick triage and revert. :thumbsup:

runtime-bot: Incident closed (temporary revert). Postmortem owner: diane.

lee: I'll attach the profiler traces and a small repro in the ticket.

diane: assigning follow-ups: PERF-487 (selector KV-awareness), PERF-488 (canary probe), TEST-1023 (regression harness). Closing thread here.
